appraisal_events.evidence: — Vous n’allez pas me faire d’observations, j’espère, me cria-t-elle, d’une voix dure et en se dégageant vivement.
appraisal_events.explanation: When the narrator suggests she reconsider for her father's sake, Gilberte cuts him off sharply and physically pulls away, dismissing his intervention with a hard tone.

appraisal_events.evidence: ce qui venait d’être réduit en poudre, ce n’était pas seulement le langoureux vieillard... c’était aussi la beauté d’une œuvre immense; the real Bergotte appears as « un homme jeune, rude, petit, râblé et myope, à nez rouge en forme de coquille de colimaçon et à barbiche noire ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's long-cherished, idealized image of Bergotte as an ethereal old sage collapses on contact with the stocky, red-nosed, bearded man actually before him, and this collapse is presented, in the narrator's own retrospective voice, as a real and painful loss rather than mere color.

status_effects.explanation: His gentle remonstrance is overridden and shut down by Gilberte's sharp, physically punctuated refusal, leaving him locally silenced.
The shattering of his imagined Bergotte leaves the narrator, by his own account, 'mortellement triste,' a direct emotional cost of the disillusionment.
Within this passage, the real Bergotte is drastically deflated in the narrator's estimation, his physical ordinariness seeming to drag down even the value of his books.
